title: Gold cross-book character identity
description: Hand-verified ground truth for which surface forms across a series' books refer to the same character (S5.14). Pinned per-book to corpus/manifest.json's pdf_sha256/page_count exactly like roster.schema.json/relations.schema.json, so a repaginated corpus fails loudly rather than silently invalidating a page-level label.

series_key.description: Must match a series_key under corpus/manifest.json's per-book series metadata.

books.description: The books this gold set spans, in series order. book_order is the key surface_forms and appears_in refer to.

book_key.description: Must match a key under corpus/manifest.json's books.

canonical.description: The one name this character is scored under project-wide.

appears_in.description: book_order values this character genuinely appears in -- not just is mentioned or remembered in.

surface_forms.description: book_order (as a string key, e.g. "1") -> surface forms this character is called by in that book.

dies_in_book.description: book_order this character's death is established in, or null. The primary cross-book blocking signal (character_death) -- a later book's same-name mention is a namesake, flashback or memory, never an automatic link, once this is set.

namesake_risk.description: True when another character in this same gold set shares a first name or surname, so a system merging them purely on string similarity is the specific failure this entry exists to catch.
